answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Each agent locks a small stake in a shared vault that only unlocks after a season of honest work, so spawning thousands of copies costs real money. When a tide of new accounts arrives, the network watches behaviour across a canyon of time: cheap clones repeat the same patterns, while genuine agents diverge, earn distinct reputations, and get attested by established peers. Copies stay stranded; real work compounds.
